haiku-low.q2: The broker redelivers it if no acknowledgement arrives within 30 s, possibly to another consumer.
haiku-low.q3: Five attempts, waits of 1, 2, 4 and 8 minutes between them, then marked failed and on-call is paged.
haiku-low.q4: shipping_update first, then order_confirmed after 3 days, then password_reset after 3 more days, only if order_confirmed p99 enqueue-to-MailRelay latency is under 60 s.
haiku-low.q5: The notification's id, passed on every send. MailRelay drops a repeat with the same key accepted within 24 hours, returning success.
haiku-low.q6: The monolith relay publishes each route=service row to notifications.requested, waits for broker confirmation, then marks it published. That mark ends its step.
haiku-low.q7: The per-type flag notify.route.<type>, read when the row is recorded; the row's route column then decides which sender takes it.
haiku-low.q8: The service's deliveries table is keyed on notification id. If the id already exists, it acknowledges and does nothing else.
haiku-low.q9: It acknowledges after inserting the deliveries row, before sending. A crash before the ack causes redelivery, which the id key makes harmless.
haiku-low.q10: In the service's deliveries table, including attempt count and next attempt time. The service's sender finds pending, due rows and applies the retry policy.
haiku-low.q11: Already-published rows finish on the service. Unpublished rows are flipped back to monolith by the relay and sent by the old worker.
haiku-low.q12: Id, type, user email and payload. The email content is rendered by the service's sender from its templates.

sonnet.q1: Durable when the row is inserted into the monolith's notifications table, committed with the caller's transaction (enqueue_notification). If that transaction fails and rolls back, no notification exists.
sonnet.q2: Redelivers it after 30 s without acknowledgement, possibly to another consumer (at-least-once).
sonnet.q3: 5 attempts, waits of 1, 2, 4 and 8 minutes between them; then the row is marked failed and on-call is paged.
sonnet.q4: shipping_update first (flag to service); after 3 days order_confirmed; after 3 more days password_reset, only if p99 enqueue-to-MailRelay latency on order_confirmed is under 60 s. (Old worker removed after password_reset runs 7 days on the service.)
sonnet.q5: The idempotency_key, which is the notification's id. If MailRelay accepted a send with the same key in the last 24 hours, it drops the new send and returns success.
sonnet.q6: Monolith inserts a row (route=service) in notifications; the monolith's relay polls unpublished service-routed rows, publishes each to the broker topic notifications.requested, waits for broker confirmation, then marks the row published. The service consumes from the broker. The monolith's part is done once the row is marked published.
sonnet.q7: The per-type route flag notify.route.<type> (monolith or service, read via flags.get). It is decided at Record time, when enqueue_notification sets the row's route column from the current flag (the relay can later flip a not-yet-published row back to monolith on rollback).
sonnet.q8: The deliveries table is keyed on the notification id: if the id already exists, the service acknowledges and does nothing else. MailRelay's idempotency key also drops duplicate sends.
sonnet.q9: It inserts the deliveries row first, then acknowledges; sending happens later by a separate sender. A crash before the acknowledgement causes redelivery, which is harmless because of the id key.
sonnet.q10: In the service's own database, in the deliveries table (attempt count and next attempt time). The service sender acts on it (picks up pending, due rows and applies the retry policy).
sonnet.q11: Rows already published stay with the service and finish there. New notifications go to the old worker. (Unpublished rows are claimed by the old worker; the relay flips their route to monolith, though the document says details of this are not settled.)
sonnet.q12: Id, type, user email and payload, published as a message. The email content is rendered by the service (sender renders the template).
